Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, declaring that the opposition lacks the political structures and capacity to pose a serious challenge to the ruling All Progressives Congress. The Senate Leader spoke on Thursday during a media parley in Abuja, where he defended the administration’s economic policies and dismissed suggestions that the President should be worried about the 2027 electoral contest. Bamidele attributed his confidence to what he described as the achievements of the Tinubu administration in its first three and a half years, particularly its economic reforms, improved investor confidence and efforts to stabilise the economy. The senator, however, acknowledged that the reforms had imposed hardship on low-income earners, artisans and other vulnerable Nigerians, insisting that the government was working to cushion their effects. He said, “I am not nursing fear that the President will lose the election. Will he win the 2027 election? Absolutely! I have no doubt that he will win.” Bamidele argued that Tinubu’s performance in office had given him an opportunity to demonstrate his leadership capacity and present his policies to Nigerians and the international investment community. He said the administration’s economic policies had improved confidence among foreign investors, adding that the inflow of capital into the country was evidence of growing confidence in the economy. According to him, the administration had also ended the practice of using money printing to finance government expenditure and had unified the foreign exchange market to eliminate multiple exchange rates. He explained that the legislature had resisted pressure to extend the subsidy beyond that period, leaving Tinubu with the option of either announcing its removal or seeking fresh legislative approval to continue funding it. “The National Assembly actually provided for oil subsidy till May of 2023. And when Asiwaju was being sworn in on May 29, 2023, he had only one option, which is either to let Nigerians know that it was gone or he would bring it back,” Bamidele said He praised the President for announcing the end of the subsidy during his inauguration, describing the decision as an expression of political courage. 2027: Atiku, Amaechi have best governance experience – Momodu Rising energy costs making housing unaffordable – Atiku Tinubu ready for more local media interviews, says Bwala Bamidele, however, admitted that the economic reforms had taken a toll on vulnerable Nigerians, saying the government was aware of the hardship and was implementing measures to provide relief. He said, “No. the truth is that our economy has survived and is on the path of growth. But it is also a fact that many Nigerians, especially the less privileged people, artisans, and low-income people are suffering based on the impact of the economic reforms.” The Senate Leader likened the economic reforms to the biblical crossing of the Red Sea, arguing that the country had passed through a difficult phase and that the next four years of Tinubu’s administration would consolidate the gains. He said, “But we have crossed that Red Sea. The Red Sea that every other previous president or administration had been afraid to take Nigerians through. “And there’s no going back to Egypt because the next four years of the Tinubu administration will witness the consolidation of the gains of this reform.” Turning to the opposition, Bamidele questioned the capacity of the African Democratic Congress and other opposition parties to challenge the APC, citing what he described as their limited electoral structures and grassroots presence. He specifically questioned the organisational strength of the ADC and the political structures available to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Bamidele argued that social media popularity could not replace the physical structures required to mobilise voters and secure electoral victories. He said, “It’s not about former vice president Atiku. My respect to him. But I know he’s a candidate of the political party that does not even have senatorial candidates, House of Reps candidates, or House of Assembly candidates in more than half of the constituencies. That is a party that we are contesting with.” He also criticised the opposition’s reliance on social media supporters, arguing that online followership did not necessarily translate into votes at polling units. The Senate Leader said the APC was approaching the 2027 election with confidence, adding that the ruling party was conscious of the economic difficulties Nigerians were experiencing and the need to address them.
